correctness.rationale: For a,b,A,B>0, d>=0, the symmetric drift is positive definite; its stationary Lyapunov matrix equations have a unique solution. Their sum covariance equals the explicitly displayed rational V(d). Exact differentiation gives V'(d)=(b-a)(BU(d)-AW(d))/[2(a+b+2d)^2(ab+(a+b)d)^2]. For a<b, the noise-ratio threshold R=U/W satisfies R'(d)=4(b-a)(a+b)(a+b+2d)(ab+(a+b)d)/W(d)^2>0, with limits a^2/b^2 and (3a+b)/(a+3b). This yields all cases, with strict global minimum only for a ratio strictly between endpoints. When a=b the summed SDE is an OU process unaffected by d. Exact independent rational solving for 480 configurations and an exact d*=1 witness were performed; finite tests are not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Four substantive comparisons and public research-index searches were conducted. The nearest pre-existing exact two-patch model (Kendall et al. 2000) assumes identical local regulation and therefore has a flat regional sum-variance, not the unequal-return phase diagram. Keeling 2000 concerns nonlinear moment-closure persistence; Loreau et al. 2003 examines nonlinear multispecies productivity stability. A 2017 paper treats homogeneous analytical spectra and heterogeneous numerical indicators, with full text unavailable. No found prior source asserts or logically implies the complete two-threshold and one-valley theorem under its stated assumptions; the Lyapunov method itself and qualitative intermediate-coupling benefits are acknowledged as old. Residual risk includes a general covariance formula or hidden stochastic-control specialization; absence of a database hit is not novelty proof.
residual_risks: The 2017 paper was evaluated from accessible text extracts only, not its complete manuscript or supplementary material.
A Lyapunov covariance theorem in linear-systems literature may contain a parameter-specialized or stronger minimizing condition without ecological terminology.
Public research indexing and available historical findings are incomplete; no human bibliographic confirmation was obtained.

value.rationale: A full if-and-only-if classification identifies precisely when intermediate migration minimizes regional abundance fluctuation variance in a natural, linear two-habitat model. The two thresholds separate forcing mainly at the faster-decaying patch (migration always harmful), balanced forcing (one global stabilizing optimum), and forcing mainly at the slower-decaying patch (migration continuously helps). This exhibits an intermediate optimum for a single species without nonlinear species sorting, and the exact d*=1 example has variance 49/100 versus 1/2 both at zero and full mixing. This is a motivated stability/management comparison, not arbitrary coefficient calculation; no empirical extrapolation or extinction claims are made.
